criteria.description: Factual fidelity to body: each sentence in the abstract must be supported by the body without inventing or misattributing facts. Defects include merging results from different GRBs, upgrading ongoing/in-progress work to completed results, adding numeric ranges or redshifts not in body, or omitting caveats the body states (e.g., unconfirmed nature of GRB000830). Several such defects should cap this criterion at 6 or below.

Coverage of problem, method and findings with appropriate uncertainty: abstract must state the problem (fast precise GRB localizations enabling OT search), the method (ESO ToO follow-up, Italian-Dutch collaboration expanding to European consortium and Large Programme from April 2000), and specific findings supported by body (e.g., first ESO ToO on GRB970111 non-detection, first OT detection GRB970228, SN1998bw/GRB980425, polarization of GRB990510/990712, redshifts including z=4.5, red afterglows GRB980329/990705, LP activations 9 times with 5 non-detections, 1 unconfirmed red object GRB000830, 3 OTs detected). Vague generic abstracts with no findings score low; detail counts only when accurate, and uncertainty language must match body.

Coherent abstract structure and length compliance: abstract is ~135 words, self-contained, logically ordered, and does not copy source tokenization spacing as content. Exceeding target by >30% (approx >175 words) must lose points on this criterion scaled to overshoot. Tokenization artifacts are minor presentation only, not content errors.
